description: A daughter is temporarily taking over care coordination for her father while her sibling travels abroad. She must reconstruct the current medication list, upcoming appointments, warning signs, and provider instructions from partial notes and text messages. All provider names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 43-year-old project coordinator managing a temporary family caregiving handoff
user_profile.context: The usual caregiver is away for three weeks and the available notes are incomplete
user_profile.communication_style: Organized but under time pressure, wants one reliable source of truth

fact_sheet.fact: The patient, Robert Miller, has a primary diagnosis of Atrial Fibrillation (AFib), confirmed on June 12, 2022.
Robert Miller has a secondary diagnosis of chronic Hypertension, managed by his Primary Care Physician, Dr. Aris Thorne.
Robert Miller was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes on March 5, 2019.
Robert Miller has Stage 3 Chronic Kidney Disease, which is monitored by Dr. Aris Thorne at Maple Creek Family Practice.
Robert Miller takes Metoprolol Succinate 50 mg, one tablet orally every morning at 8:00 AM, for heart rate and blood pressure control.
Robert Miller takes Eliquis (Apixaban) 5 mg, one tablet orally twice daily at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM, to prevent blood clots.
Robert Miller takes Lisinopril 20 mg, one tablet orally every morning at 8:00 AM, for hypertension.
Robert Miller takes Metformin 1000 mg, one tablet orally twice daily with breakfast and dinner, to manage blood sugar.
Robert Miller takes Atorvastatin 40 mg, one tablet orally every evening at 9:00 PM, for high cholesterol.
All prescriptions for Robert Miller are filled at Grove Street Pharmacy, located at 124 Grove St, Pinewood City.
The prescription for Eliquis (Apixaban) is due for a refill on October 28, 2024; the prescription number is RX789012.
Robert Miller has a documented allergy to Penicillin, which causes a severe skin rash (hives).
Robert Miller must follow a low-sodium diet, with a daily limit of 1,500 mg of sodium, as per instructions from his cardiologist, Dr. Petrova.
Robert Miller's exercise plan consists of walking for 30 minutes at a moderate pace, at least 5 days per week.
Due to his kidney condition, Robert Miller's total daily fluid intake should be limited to 2 liters (approximately 64 ounces).
To manage his Type 2 Diabetes, Robert Miller's diet should limit carbohydrates to 45-60 grams per meal.
Robert Miller must check his blood pressure at home every morning before taking medication; the target reading is below 130/80 mmHg.
Robert Miller must monitor his blood glucose levels twice daily: before breakfast (fasting) and 2 hours after dinner. The target fasting level is 80-130 mg/dL.
An upcoming appointment with cardiologist Dr. Lena Petrova is scheduled for November 5, 2024, at 10:30 AM at the Northwood Cardiology Center.
A follow-up appointment with PCP Dr. Aris Thorne for a routine check-up and lab work review is scheduled for December 3, 2024, at 2:00 PM.
The patient portal for Maple Creek Family Practice is accessible at https://mychart.maplecreek.health with the username 'RMiller1948'.
For non-urgent questions, Dr. Aris Thorne's medical assistant, Jane Calloway, can be reached at (555) 234-5678 during office hours.
The primary caregiver, David Miller, will be traveling abroad and unreachable from October 15, 2024, to November 7, 2024.
Warning signs of a stroke requiring an immediate 911 call include facial drooping, arm weakness, or speech difficulty (F.A.S.T. acronym).
If Robert Miller's blood pressure reading is consistently above 180/120 mmHg, call the Northwood Cardiology Center's on-call nurse at (555) 876-5432.
Symptoms of severe hypoglycemia (low blood sugar), such as confusion, unresponsiveness, or loss of consciousness, require an immediate 911 call.
In case of a fall, even if Robert appears uninjured, Dr. Thorne's office must be notified within 24 hours due to the increased risk of internal bleeding while on Eliquis.
